topic: What happens if you nap every afternoon?
title: What afternoon naps do
hook: What happens if you nap every afternoon?

beats.label: 0 MIN
beats.line: Without a nap, the after-lunch dip can leave you yawning at your desk.

beats.label: 10 MIN
beats.line: A ten-minute nap can make you sharper almost right away.

beats.label: 26 MIN
beats.line: Twenty-six minutes: in a NASA study, that nap made pilots far more alert.

beats.label: 60 MIN
beats.line: Sixty minutes can pull you into deep sleep, and you may wake up groggy.

beats.label: 90 MIN
beats.line: Ninety minutes is about one full sleep cycle, and you may even dream.

end.line: How long do your naps usually last?

description: From ten minutes to ninety: what different afternoon nap lengths do to your brain.

facts.claim: Alertness naturally dips in the early afternoon (about 1-3 p.m.), largely from the body clock; the dip shows up even without lunch.
facts.source: Monk, The post-lunch dip in performance, Clin Sports Med 2005 (PubMed 15892914) / Mayo Clinic (Napping)

facts.claim: In a sleep-lab study, a 10-minute afternoon nap improved alertness and performance immediately, with benefits lasting up to about 155 minutes.
NASA study of long-haul pilots: those given a cockpit nap slept about 26 minutes on average; performance improved 34% and physiological alertness up to 54%.
facts.source: NASA Ames (Rosekind et al., 1994-95) / Sleep Foundation (NASA nap)

facts.claim: Longer naps make deep sleep and grogginess on waking (sleep inertia) more likely; a 30-minute nap already caused sleep inertia in the lab.
facts.source: Mayo Clinic (Napping: do's and don'ts) / Brooks & Lack 2006

facts.claim: A sleep cycle lasts roughly 90 minutes; REM sleep, when vivid dreaming is most common, first occurs about 90 minutes after falling asleep.
